correctness.rationale: For nonzero real x, smoothness of \(\ell_4^3\) gives the unique norming functional x_i^3/Σx_j^4. The exactly checked quartic Vandermonde factorization reduces the quotient to the sum t, normalized squared deviation s=1 and cubic invariant q. Newton/discriminant identities give \(\Delta^2=1/2-3q^2\) and establish all q in the resulting closed interval are achievable. Fixed-t optimization over u=−√6q has a unique maximum u=B/A because \(A-B\ge7/18\). The global t-optimization has the single positive critical \(r=(\sqrt6-2)/6\) and zero endpoint limits, giving \(v^2=3\sqrt6/256\). Equality at both strict optima yields precisely the displayed cubic-root orbit; the exact identity checker and 60,000 diagnostic comparisons completed successfully. Only real ℓ4 and the specified matrix are proved.

value.rationale: Two noncommuting conditional expectations first occur on the minimal three-atom probability space, making their commutator a canonical operator rather than an arbitrary matrix slice. Its real Hilbert numerical radius is zero because the commutator is skew-adjoint, yet the first algebraically tractable non-Hilbert even exponent p=4 yields the explicit positive radius \(\sqrt{3\sqrt6}/16\). The sharp global inequality, strict unique optimizing invariants and full norming-vector orbit give substantive geometry of numerical ranges beyond a numerical computation, and a precise test case for quantitative non-Hilbert conditional-expectation estimates. No general numerical-index theorem or other exponent is claimed.
